findings.title: Keep the reviewer code outside the PR checkout
findings.whyItBreaks: The job checks out the PR head and then installs and executes its package and src/cli.ts. An internal PR can alter either path, so arbitrary PR code runs on the self-hosted runner with GH_TOKEN explicitly granted pull-requests:write and checks:write; it can forge review results or compromise the runner.

findings.title: Restore a checkout containing Needlefish's manifest
findings.whyItBreaks: The checked-out head tree contains only .github/workflows/review.yml and .needlefish/answers.json; it has no package.json or pnpm-lock.yaml. Running pnpm install --frozen-lockfile in the repository root therefore fails before the review command can run.

facts.meaning: The workflow executes Needlefish's reviewer implementation from the untrusted PR-head checkout.
The PR-controlled reviewer can write pull-request reviews or checks.

findings.title: Restore a trusted reviewer checkout
findings.whyItBreaks: A same-repository PR can supply package scripts and src/cli.ts in its head commit. This job checks out that head, runs pnpm install, then executes it with a token allowed to write pull-request reviews and checks. The PR can therefore forge or suppress its own review result.

findings.title: Provide the tool files before invoking them
findings.whyItBreaks: The reviewed head contains only .github/workflows/review.yml and .needlefish/answers.json; it has no package.json, pnpm-lock.yaml, or src/cli.ts. Consequently pnpm install fails before a review can run (and the tsx invocation would also reference a nonexistent file).

findings.title: Restore an isolated trusted reviewer checkout
findings.whyItBreaks: The checkout at the PR-head ref is now also the tool source, so any same-repository PR can modify src/cli.ts to suppress findings or use the injected write-capable GH_TOKEN to forge review output.
